h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר מ׳ Pesach — Maamar Mem

p: שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים תֹּאכַל מַצּוֹת וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי עֲצֶרֶת לַה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ וְגוֹמֵר
"Six days you shall eat matzos, and on the seventh day shall be an assembly (atzeres) to Hashem your God, etc."
(דְּבָרִים ט"ז, ח'),
(Devarim 16:8),
וְלָמְדוּ מִזֶּה
and the Sages derived from this
(פְּסָחִים ק"כ.):
(Pesachim 120a):
מַה שְּׁבִיעִי רְשׁוּת אַף שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים רְשׁוּת.
"Just as on the seventh day eating matzah is optional, so too on all six days it is optional, etc."

וְצָרִיךְ לְהָבִין לָמָּה נִכְתַּב זֶה הַלִּימּוּד שֶׁאֲכִילַת מַצָּה רְשׁוּת בַּשְּׁבִיעִי וְשֶׁיִּלְמְדוּ מִזֶּה לְכָל הַשִּׁשָּׁה יָמִים בְּ"דָבָר שֶׁהָיָה בִּכְלָל וְכוּלֵּי"—הֲוָה לֵיהּ לוֹמַר בְּכָל הַשִּׁשָּׁה יָמִים!

Now one must understand why the Torah recorded that eating matzah is optional on the seventh day so that we derive from it for all six days via the hermeneutical rule of "anything that was included in a general statement, etc."—it could simply have stated it directly regarding all six days!
וְהִנֵּה בִּשְׁמִינִי עֲצֶרֶת כְּתִיב
Now regarding Shemini Atzeres it is written
(בְּמִדְבַּר כ"ט, ל"ה):
(Bamidbar 29:35):
עֲצֶרֶת תִּהְיֶה לָכֶם,
"An assembly (atzeres) shall it be to you (lachem),"
וְכָאן כְּתִיב: עֲצֶרֶת לַה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ, וְנֶחְלְקוּ בָּזֶה רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
whereas here [on the seventh day of Pesach] it is written "an assembly to Hashem your God," over which Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua disputed
(פְּסָחִים ס"ח:).
(Pesachim 68b).
וְהִנֵּה בְּתַנְחוּמָא
And in Midrash Tanchuma
(פִּנְחָס ט"ו)
(Pinchas 15)
אִיתָא עַל שְׁמִינִי עֲצֶרֶת: וְהָיְתָה רְאוּיָה לִהְיוֹת אַחַר הֶחָג חֲמִשִּׁים יוֹם, כְּשֵׁם שֶׁעֲצֶרֶת אַחַר הֶחָג חֲמִשִּׁים יוֹם, אֶלָּא אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: חֹרֶף הוּא וְכוּלֵּי

it is stated regarding Shemini Atzeres that by right it should have been placed fifty days after Sukkos, just as Shavuos (Atzeres) is fifty days after Pesach, except the Holy One, blessed is He, said, "It is winter [so I will not burden you to travel again], etc."
נִרְאֶה מִזֶּה שֶׁחַג שָׁבוּעוֹת הוּא כְּמוֹ שְׁמִינִי עֲצֶרֶת אַחַר סוּכּוֹת, כֵּן שָׁבוּעוֹת אַחַר פֶּסַח.
from which it is evident that just as Shemini Atzeres follows Sukkos, so Shavuos follows Pesach.
וּבֶאֱמֶת בַּתּוֹרָה לֹא נִקְרָא כְּלָל שָׁבוּעוֹת בְּשֵׁם "עֲצֶרֶת", רַק שְׁבִיעִי שֶׁל פֶּסַח נִקְרָא בַּתּוֹרָה "עֲצֶרֶת", רַק בִּלְשׁוֹן חֲזַ"ל נִקְרָא שָׁבוּעוֹת "עֲצֶרֶת".
And in truth, in the Written Torah Shavuos is never called Atzeres—only the seventh day of Pesach is called Atzeres in the Torah—whereas in the parlance of the Sages Shavuos is called Atzeres.
וְהָאֲרִי הַקָּדוֹשׁ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה כָּתַב דְּ"עֲצֶרֶת" הוּא לְשׁוֹן קְלִיטָה, שֶׁהַקְּדוּשָּׁה נִקְלֶטֶת אָז.
Now the holy Arizal, of blessed memory, wrote that atzeres denotes "absorption/retention," meaning the holiness of the festival is absorbed and internalized then.
וְיִתָּכֵן דִּקְדוּשַׁת הַפֶּסַח מִצַּד יִשְׂרָאֵל עִיקַּר הַקְּלִיטָה בְּחַג שָׁבוּעוֹת, וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי נִקְרָא בִּלְשׁוֹן חֲכָמִים שָׁבוּעוֹת "עֲצֶרֶת",

And it may be explained that from Israel's side, the primary absorption of the holiness of Pesach takes place on the festival of Shavuos, which is why in the language of the Sages Shavuos is called Atzeres,
וּכְמוֹ כֵן בִּשְׁמִינִי עֲצֶרֶת הוּא "עֲצֶרֶת לָכֶם", קְלִיטַת קְדוּשַׁת חַג הַסּוּכּוֹת;
and likewise on Shemini Atzeres it is "an assembly to you (lachem)," the absorption of the holiness of Sukkos [into Israel];
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מִצַּד ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ נִקְרָא שְׁבִיעִי שֶׁל פֶּסַח "עֲצֶרֶת לַה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ", שֶׁהָיָה צוֹפֶה תֵּיכֶף בִּשְׁבִיעִי שֶׁל פֶּסַח שֶׁכְּבָר נִקְלְטָה הַקְּדוּשָּׁה דְּחַג הַפֶּסַח.

whereas from the side of Hashem, may He be blessed, the seventh day of Pesach is called "an assembly to Hashem your God," because He foresaw immediately on the seventh day of Pesach that the holiness of Pesach was already absorbed.

דִּקְדוּשַׁת הַפֶּסַח אָמַר רַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה בְּשֵׁם רַבֵּינוּ רַבִּי רַב בּוּנָם מִפְּשִׁיסְחָא זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה שֶׁהוּא כְּמוֹ רְאִיַּת חָתָן וְכַלָּה, וְשָׁבוּעוֹת הוּא הַקִּנְיָן.

For our holy master said in the name of our master Rabbi Bunim of Peshischa, may their righteous and holy memories be for a blessing, that the holiness of Pesach is like the initial betrothal gaze of bridegroom and bride, while Shavuos is the actual marriage acquisition.

וְהִנֵּה בְּפֶסַח, אַף שֶׁהָיָה אָז גַּם כֵּן בְּעַתִּיקָא—שֶׁאָז הָיָה מַכַּת בְּכוֹרוֹת, מַכָּה עֲשִׂירִית, שֶׁאָז יָצְאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵהַקְּלִיפָּה מִמִּדָּה עֲשִׂירִית שֶׁהוּא רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם וְנִכְנְסוּ לִקְדוּשָּׁה בְּמִדָּה רִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁהוּא כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן—אַךְ לֹא הָיָה רַק לְפִי שָׁעָה,

Now on the first night of Pesach, although they also reached Atika—for then was the Plague of the Firstborn, the tenth plague, when Israel emerged from the tenth husk ("the first of nations") and entered holiness at the topmost attribute, Kesser Elyon—nevertheless that was only temporary,
שֶׁאַחֲרֵי זֶה הָיָה הַקִּטְרוּג עוֹד: מַה נִּשְׁתַּנּוּ אֵלּוּ מֵאֵלּוּ, עַד עַכְשָׁיו אֵלּוּ עוֹבְדֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְאַתָּה קוֹרֵעַ לָהֶם אֶת הַיָּם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה
for afterward there was still the prosecution "How are these different from those? Until now these were idol worshippers and You split the Sea for them!" as they said in Midrash Rabbah
(שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה כ"א, ז')
(Shemos Rabbah 21:7)
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
and in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' ק"ע:).
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּשְׁעַת קְרִיעַת יַם סוּף שֶׁאָז הָיָה הָרְאִיָּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
Not so at the time of the Splitting of the Sea [the seventh day of Pesach], when there was direct prophetic vision, as they said
(מְכִילְתָּא הַשִּׁירָה ג' וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ב' ס"ד:):
(Mechilta Shirah 3, and in the holy Zohar, Vol. 2, 64b):
רָאֲתָה שִׁפְחָה עַל הַיָּם מַה שֶּׁלֹּא רָאָה יְחֶזְקֵאל
"A maidservant saw at the Sea what Yechezkel did not see"
וְאַף שֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ נֶעְלַם מֵהֶם, דִּכְתִיב
and even though afterward it became concealed from them, as it is written
(שְׁמוֹת ט"ו, כ"ב):
(Shemos 15:22):
וַיֵּלְכוּ שְׁלֹשֶׁת יָמִים וְלֹא מָצְאוּ מָיִם
"And they went three days and found no water"
וְאֵין מַיִם אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא
and "water" means nothing other than Torah, as they said in the Gemara
(בָּבָא קַמָּא פ"ב.)
(Bava Kamma 82a)
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
and in the holy Zohar
וְכִי מַאן יָהֵיב לְהוֹ אוֹרַיְיתָא הָכָא וְכוּלֵּי? וְאוֹלִיפְנָא דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא תּוֹרָה אִיקְרֵי וְכוּלֵּי
"Who gave them the Torah here, etc.? And we have learned that the Holy One, blessed is He, is called Torah, etc."
עַל כָּל פָּנִים נִשְׁאַר לָהֶם הַתְּשׁוּקָה וְהַחֵשֶׁק, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ.
in any event, there remained within them the longing and yearning [for that Divine light], as brought in the holy Zohar.
וְאָמְרוּ בְּשֵׁם הַבַּעַל שֵׁם טוֹב שֶׁהִפְלִיא חוֹזֶק הַחֲסִידוּת בִּתְחִילָּתוֹ, וּמֵרַבֵּינוּ רַבִּי רַב בּוּנָם זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה אָמְרוּ שֶׁאָמַר עַל זֶה מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר

And they cite in the name of the Baal Shem Tov that he marveled at the intensity of a person's devotion at the very beginning of his spiritual path, and from our master Rabbi Bunim, may his righteous and holy memory be for a blessing, they cite on this what is said
(קֹהֶלֶת ז', י'):
(Koheles 7:10):
אַל תֹּאמַר שֶׁהַיָּמִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים טוֹבִים מֵאֵלֶּה כִּי לֹא מֵחָכְמָה שָׁאַלְתָּ זֹאת וְכוּלֵּי
"Do not say, 'Why were the former days better than these?' for it is not out of wisdom that you ask this, etc."

דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁמִּתְּחִילָּה מַרְאֶה ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ לְהָאָדָם בִּשְׁאֵלָה מַה שֶּׁיָּכוֹל לְהַשִּׂיג אַחַר כָּךְ בִּיגִיעָתוֹ, וְאַחֲרֵי זֶה מְסַלֵּק מִמֶּנּוּ אוֹתוֹ הָאוֹר כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּקְנֶה זֹאת בִּיגִיעוֹ;

meaning that at first Hashem, may He be blessed, shows a person on loan what he is capable of attaining afterward through his own toil, and then He withdraws that light from him so that he may acquire it permanently through his own exertion;
וְאָמַר רַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה עַל זֶה שֶׁכְּשִׁיעוּר שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהַשִּׂיג אַחַר כָּךְ בִּיגִיעוֹ כָּכָה מַרְאֶה לוֹ ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּתְּחִילָּה.
and our holy master commented on this that in exact proportion to what a person can later achieve through his toil, so does Hashem, may He be blessed, show him at the outset.
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי מִצַּד יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא עִיקַּר עֲצֶרֶת בְּחַג שָׁבוּעוֹת שֶׁהָיָה אָז מַתַּן תּוֹרָה
Therefore, from Israel's side, the true Atzeres (absorption) is on the festival of Shavuos, when the Giving of the Torah took place

וְלוּלָא הַקִּלְקוּל: אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי אֱלֹהִים אַתֶּם, וְהָיָה אָז הַתִּיקּוּן בִּשְׁלֵימוּת, וְאָז הוּא עֲצֶרֶת מִצַּד יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְלָכֵן נִקְרָא בִּלְשׁוֹן חֲזַ"ל שָׁבוּעוֹת "עֲצֶרֶת", וְאָז מַקְרִיבִין שְׂאוֹר וְחָמֵץ, אַף שֶׁבְּכָל הַשָּׁנָה אָסוּר לְהַקְרִיב שְׂאוֹר, אַךְ אָז כְּבָר נִתְבָּרֵר שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁמִּיעוּטָן יָפֶה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת

and had it not been for the sin of the Golden Calf, "I said, you are angelic beings" would have endured in complete perfection, and then it is Atzeres from Israel's side, which is why the Sages call Shavuos Atzeres and why we offer leaven and chametz on it—for even though all year round it is forbidden to offer leaven, then it has already been refined into "leaven of which a small amount is beneficial," as they said in Berachos
אֲבָל ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ הֵעִיד עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּשְׁבִיעִי שֶׁל פֶּסַח שֶׁכְּבָר נִקְלַט אֶצְלָם הַקְּדוּשָּׁה: וְרָאֲתָה שִׁפְחָה וְכוּלֵּי, וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: עֲצֶרֶת לַה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ;

However, Hashem, may He be blessed, testified concerning Israel on the seventh day of Pesach that the holiness was already absorbed within them—"and a maidservant saw, etc."—and this is why it says "an assembly to Hashem your God";

מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן שְׁמִינִי עֲצֶרֶת נֶאֱמַר: עֲצֶרֶת תִּהְיֶה לָכֶם, שֶׁאָז נִקְלַט הַקְּדוּשָּׁה מֵחַג הַסּוּכּוֹת אַף מִצַּד יִשְׂרָאֵל, וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי שִׁינָּה הַכָּתוּב בִּשְׁמִינִי עֲצֶרֶת: תִּהְיֶה לָכֶם, וְכָאן: עֲצֶרֶת לַה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ.

whereas on Shemini Atzeres it is stated "an assembly shall it be to you (lachem)," because then the holiness from Sukkos is absorbed even from Israel's side—and therefore Scripture varied its wording on Shemini Atzeres to "shall it be to you," while here it says "an assembly to Hashem your God."
וְזֶה שֶׁזָּכַר כָּאן שֶׁאֲכִילַת מַצָּה רְשׁוּת
And this is why it mentions here [on the seventh day] that eating matzah is optional
שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת אִם הָיָה כָּאן הַקִּנְיָן וְהַקְּלִיטָה הָיָה מוּתָּר כָּאן אַף אֲכִילַת חָמֵץ כְּמוֹ בְּחַג הַשָּׁבוּעוֹת,
for in truth, had the final acquisition and absorption occurred here, even eating chametz would have been permitted here just as on Shavuos,
רַק מִטַּעַם כֵּיוָן שֶׁמִּצַּד יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא נִגְמַר הַקְּלִיטָה עֲדַיִין אָז, שֶׁאַחֲרֵי זֶה נִסְתַּר מֵהֶם הָאוֹר כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, עֲדַיִין נוֹהֵג אִיסּוּר חָמֵץ,
only because from Israel's side the absorption was not yet completed then—since afterward the light became hidden from them, as mentioned above—the prohibition of chametz still applies,

אַךְ עַל כָּל פָּנִים כֵּיוָן שֶׁהוּא "עֲצֶרֶת לַה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ", לִימְּדָה הַתּוֹרָה כָּאן שֶׁאֲכִילַת מַצָּה רְשׁוּת, וּמִמֶּנּוּ נִלְמַד לִשְׁאָר הַיָּמִים שֶׁהוּא רְשׁוּת בְּ"דָבָר שֶׁהָיָה בִּכְלָל וְכוּלֵּי".

yet in any case, since it is "an assembly to Hashem your God," the Torah teaches here that eating matzah is optional, and from it we derive for all the remaining days that it is optional via "anything that was included in a general statement, etc."

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 120a — "'Six days you shall eat matzos, and on the seventh day shall be an assembly to Hashem your God': just as the seventh day is optional, so too the six days are optional." Rashbam (who comments on this chapter in place of Rashi): one may eat meat without bread on those days, or even fast; the seventh day left the general rule to teach about all of it. Only the first night is obligatory.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Kalonymus Kalman Shapira, Derech HaMelech, Acharon shel Pesach 5690 — “On Shavuos Israel received the light within themselves through their service, by the counting; not so Pesach, where the light came as a new creation. We see the light concealed, yet a power remains to reveal holiness by leaping. By strict measure one could rise only little by little; but on Pesach they were given this power, so that a man in any state can spring far above his level. And although he does not remain on that high rung, since he was absorbed in supernal holiness for a moment, he already begins from then on to serve Hashem and to rise greatly.” Connection: He opens with the same contrast of ‘an assembly to Hashem your God’ and ‘to you,’ and likewise holds that Pesach's light, granted from Above and then concealed, is absorbed through later service; he adds that the brief leap itself empowers the climb.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sod Yesharim, Acharon shel Pesach 14 — “On Pesach, the beginning of the festivals, a person becomes a vessel to receive His light; therefore it is written ‘Six days you shall eat matzos’: a person must contract himself to be a vessel ready to receive inner light from Hashem. And this is ‘just as the seventh is optional’: after a person has contracted himself, he can afterward enter matters that need refinement, as it is written, ‘Go, eat your bread with joy… for God has already accepted your deeds.’ ‘So too the six days are optional’: all six days were clarified, that all his contractions in them were by his own choice and good will.” Connection: The same derasha of Pesachim 120a; where the maamar ties “optional” to holiness already absorbed in Hashem’s sight, it reads the seventh day as showing that the six days’ restraint was freely chosen.
